# Add a package to a muxt.json workspace: muxt generate config, muxt generate package,
# muxt generate def, then muxt generate from the muxt.json directory.

muxt generate config

# A second run refuses and names the file.
! muxt generate config
cmpenv stderr want-config-again.txt

muxt generate package workspace
stdout 'wrote muxt.json: packages\["example.com/m/workspace"\]'

# The route goes in a template file; the method stub the receiver lacks goes
# to stdout, and the person appends it to the Go file.
cd workspace
muxt generate def 'GET /foo Index()' --output-file=index.gohtml
cp stdout stub.txt
cat workspace.go stub.txt
cp stdout workspace.go
cp ../workspace_test.txt workspace_test.go
cd ..

# With no flags, muxt generate writes every package the muxt.json lists.
muxt generate

# The same directory checks every entry the muxt.json lists.
muxt check
stdout '^ok: 1 template$'

exec go test ./...

-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.22
-- want-config-again.txt --
Error: $WORK/muxt.json already configures this directory; add a package with: muxt generate package NAME
-- workspace_test.txt --
package workspace

import (
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"testing"
)

func TestIndex(t *testing.T) {
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	TemplateRoutes(mux, T{})

	rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
	mux.ServeHTTP(rec, httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/foo", nil))

	if got, want := rec.Result().StatusCode, http.StatusNoContent; got != want {
		t.Errorf("GET /foo status = %d, want %d", got, want)
	}
}
